subject: Post-call: Dedicated pool qualification and ops runbook request
messages:
From: Samuel Jones <samuel.jones@stratagemhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from today's discovery — dedicated pool sizing & isolation

Vivek / Ben —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Quick recap from our side so we're aligned before you send a proposal:

- Pain: Our inference costs have spiked during weekday peaks; we need predictable unit cost for production LLM endpoints (HIPAA workloads).
- Isolation requirement: must be single-tenant; customer PHI cannot touch multi-tenant shared pools.
- Scale: baseline throughput ~120 qps (short requests), peak bursts up to ~450 qps for scheduled batches; we'd like graceful burst into shared capacity if possible but only after fail-safe tenant isolation guarantees.
- SLA ask: 99.9% uptime, P95 latency < 250ms for short-context queries; longer-context jobs can be best-effort.

Two asks from our side: 1) can you provide a sizing recommendation (GPU type & count) and an ops runbook for failover/burst? 2) security evidence (SOC2 Type II scope + any HIPAA attestation or BAAs) we can show legal.

I attached a high-level network diagram and our internal load profile. Happy to hop on another 30m if helpful.

—Sam
Stratagem Health — Senior Director, Platform Engineering

Attachments: Stratagem_NETWORK_DIAGRAM.png (PNG, 1.2MB)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Jones <samuel.jones@stratagemhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery — dedicated pool sizing & isolation

Sam —

Appreciate the clear summary. Below is our post-call recap and an initial operational proposal. I want to make sure the ask you sent maps to the right commitments from Redwood.

Key pain points we heard
- Cost volatility during bursts; you need predictable per-token economics for forecasting.
- Absolute isolation for PHI workloads; auditability + KMS controls required.
- Fast tail-latency (P95) for short requests during business hours.

Proposed dedicated architecture (initial guess; we'll refine after telemetry review)
- Dedicated single-tenant pool: 8x A100 80GB (reserved) to meet baseline 120 qps with room for steady growth.
- Burst policy: allow overflow into pre-warmed shared burst lanes with strict KV-cache boundary and network path separation; we will gate burst with tenant-level policy and circuit-breaker to prevent cross-tenant resource bleed.
- Autoscale window: signal-based scaling on sustained 95th percentile CPU/GPU utilization > 75% for 5 minutes; target spin-up time 90–120s.
- SLA targets (proposal): 99.9% monthly uptime for API surface; P95 latency target < 200ms for short-context endpoints under reserved pool.

Operational runbook highlights (we will deliver full ops runbook with SLOs and playbooks)
- Incident detection: synthetic checks, token-level latency tracing, reserved-pool utilization alerts.
- Failover: automatic redirect to warmed standby pool in same region with degradation notice to application.
- Security: customer-managed KMS, VPC peering/VPN, audit logs for model invocations and key access.

Open questions we need from you to firm sizing & SOW
1) Average token length and distribution for short vs. long queries (you sent peak qps but not median tokens per request).
2) Acceptable cost vs. latency tradeoff if we need to reduce reserved nodes (example: keep latency p95 at <250ms but cost lower).
3) Legal: timeline for executing a BAA and whether your procurement requires a specific contract clause we should pre-surface.

Attached: capacity-worksheet.xlsx (simple model for us to iterate on).

Next steps
- I'll run the worksheet with our infra team and share a first-draft SOW + preliminary pricing by EOD Monday (May 10).
- Ben will draft a short ops-runbook outline and Priya will pull SOC2 artifacts that map to your questions.

If that timeline works, we'll lock Milestone 0 (proof-of-fit) as a 4-week onboarding program with acceptance criteria for throughput and isolation.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity-worksheet.xlsx
From: Samuel Jones <samuel.jones@stratagemhealth.com>

Date: Sat, 8 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery — dedicated pool sizing & isolation

Thanks Vivek — that looks mostly aligned. Quick replies inline:

- Tokens: short queries ~18 tokens median (mostly single-turn prompts), long jobs ~1.2k tokens on batch runs.
- We can tolerate P95 up to 250ms during business hours if it reduces cost; prefer <200ms if within the same price band.
- Procurement: we need a BAA signed before any PHI flows; procurement can do 30-day review but prefer to front-load security artifacts.

Please send the SOC2 Type II scope and any relevant pen-test summary. Also, if you can put a DocuSign link for the BAA + SOW draft, that will speed legal review.

—Sam

Sam — thanks for the quick clarifications. Summary of commitments and owners below; we aim to deliver the items to you by Monday EOD (May 10):

Action items (owner — eta)
- SOW first draft + preliminary pricing (Vivek) — 2027-05-10 17:00 PDT — includes proposal for 8x A100 reserved pool + burst policy and SLA language.
- Ops runbook outline (Ben Carter) — 2027-05-10 17:00 PDT — incident response, failover steps, warm-standby policy.
- SOC2 artifacts & pen-test summary (Priya Natarajan) — 2027-05-10 17:00 PDT — we'll include scope, auditor report summary, and description of control mappings relevant to HIPAA.
- Legal pre-review and BAA template (Laura Bennett) — 2027-05-10 12:00 PDT — will surface any non-standard redlines early.

Deliverables we'll attach in the next email: SOW-draft-v0.1.pdf, ops-runbook-outline.docx, SOC2-summary.pdf, and a DocuSign link for the BAA + SOW.

Proposed Milestone 0 (proof-of-fit)
- 4 weeks: setup reserved pool, test baseline 120 qps for short queries, validate isolation with audit logs and KMS proof, and demonstrate controlled burst to shared lanes without cross-tenant exposure. Acceptance: throughput + P95 latency <= agreed target, evidence of audit trail.

If you're good with this, I'll send the package Monday and propose a 30-min legal + procurement touchpoint later that day.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
